doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Early sewer gigs for a buck, and the clubs she remembers
summary: Before the High Jinx she did dives for a dollar and once a quarter because she ate three hot dogs; she lists the Silhouette, Capital Lounge and others.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And that was your first paid gig I suppose.
No, I had done some sewers before that for a buck and one gig I worked, I got only a quarter, ‘cause the broad said I had eaten three hot dogs. So, it’s 35 cents for three, so the quarter was my pay.
Now, you mention the sewers, the clubs. Do you remember the names of any of them?
Like, the Silhouette, The Capital Lounge, Elmer’s, The Brass Rail, The Bar Music, places like that.
